key_finding: Lead-lag verdict: ISM Services PMI does not lead SPY at monthly frequency. Toda-Yamamoto Granger ISM Services->SPY is not significant at any lag 1-12, while SPY->ISM Services is significant at every lag, consistent with a sentiment/coincident survey already reflected in equities. The tournament winner (gap_50/T3_zscore_neg_1.0/P1_long_cash pro/L3/LB120) is countercyclical (long SPY only when lagged PMI gap-to-50 is unusually weak versus its rolling window): OOS Sharpe 1.54 vs B&H 0.88, max DD -3.8% vs -23.9%, but it gives up return (9.8% vs 15.1%), bootstrap p=0.073 (n.s. at 5%), and a structural break is flagged at 2009-03-31 — treat as a drawdown-control search result, not validated standalone alpha.
mechanism: Natural prior is procyclical: an ISM Services PMI above 50 signals services expansion and should usually align with risk-on equity conditions. The searched winner is the opposite: it buys SPY after unusually weak services sentiment, which is best treated as a fragile maximum-pessimism or mean-reversion hypothesis rather than proof that PMI leads equities.
caveats: Toda-Yamamoto Granger causality is reverse-dominant: SPY predicts ISM Services PMI at lags 1-12, while ISM Services PMI predicts SPY at no tested lag.
In-sample Sharpe is negative (-0.11) while OOS Sharpe is 1.54, an inversion that points to fragility rather than stability.
OOS performance is episode_concentrated and likely rides specific episodes, especially the COVID services collapse and recovery.
Bootstrap p-value is 0.073, so the winner is not significant at the 5% level.
Evidence status is found_in_search, not a fresh final exam; confidence remains low.
Structural break flagged at 2009-03 and the overlay gives up annual return versus buy-and-hold (9.8% vs 15.1%) in exchange for lower drawdown.
narrative_summary: ISM Services PMI is economically procyclical, but the searched SPY rule is contrarian: it buys after services sentiment is unusually weak. The result is interesting as a drawdown-management overlay, not as evidence that the survey leads the S&P 500.
